Render a CATLAS stimulus using magick

Source: R/stims-methods.R
render_stimulus.catlas_stimulus.Rd

Binds a text label to a source image, allowing control over layout and typography.

Usage

# S3 method for class 'catlas_stimulus'
render_stimulus(
  x,
  ...,
  width = 200,
  height = 200,
  font_size = 32,
  font_family = NULL,
  label_colour = "black",
  label_position = c("bottom", "top"),
  label_shift = c(0, 0),
  background = "#c1c1c1"
)

Arguments

x

A catlas_stimulus object.

...

Currently unused; reserved for future expansion.

width, height

numeric(1). Output dimensions in pixels.

font_size

numeric(1). Label font size in points.

font_family

character(1) or NULL. Font family name (NULL = auto-detect by platform).

label_colour

character(1). Text colour.

label_position

character(1). Vertical label placement, "bottom" (default) or "top". Partial matching supported.

label_shift

numeric(2). Horizontal and vertical offset of the label.

background

character(1). Background colour.

Value

A magick-image object (i.e., S3 class from magick).

Details

The label is vertically aligned to prevent overlap. When placed at the bottom, the text baseline sits just above the canvas edge; when placed at the top, the text top sits just below the canvas edge. Image scaling preserves aspect ratio while fitting the available space.

See also

Other stimuli: catlas_stimulus(), print.catlas_stimulus(), render_stimulus(), write_stimulus()

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
# A minimal white PNG to satisfy the file-existence check
tmp <- tempfile(fileext = ".png")
magick::image_write(magick::image_blank(1L, 1L, "white"), tmp)

stim <- catlas_stimulus(
  label      = "Xyline",
  image_path = tmp,
  type       = "cue"
)

# Default: label below the image
img_bottom  <- render_stimulus(stim)

# Label above image
img_top <- render_stimulus(stim, label_position = "top")
} # }
